elements.element: Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence
elements.evidence: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence
professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000

elements.element: Cyber/privacy USD 5M where Vendor processes Customer Data
elements.evidence: cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000 where Garman processes Sparkling data

elements.element: Workers' compensation as required by law
elements.evidence: workers' compensation insurance as required by law
Garman shall provide certificates of insurance to Sparkling on request
errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000 (exceeds USD 1M)
cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000 (exceeds USD 2M)

reasons: All six preferred atomic elements (CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber 5M for Customer Data processing, workers' comp per law, certificates on request) are expressly present in the inserted paragraph (k), so the locked preferred level is complete.

The insertion is an appropriate concise cure for an absent clause: the Agreement contained no insurance covenant and the redline leaves the untouched entire-agreement paragraph (j) fully effective, introducing no contradiction or dangling mechanic.

Minimality fails only on the added post-termination coverage tail 'and for one (1) year thereafter', which is not part of the preferred position and extends the obligation beyond what is needed to complete the selected level; delete it or leave the covenant coterminous with the term.

Noted, not a deviation: the clause uses lowercase 'Sparkling data' rather than a defined 'Customer Data' term; since no definitions were resolved this creates no undefined defined-term, but aligning it to the Agreement's data terminology would be cleaner.
